sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption uses its community survey to examine perceptions of corruption, awareness of the Commission and willingness to report wrongdoing.
sentences.support: The CAS directly assesses an individual’s understanding of corruption and their willingness to report it.

sentences.text: The 2012 telephone survey received 506 responses from NSW adults and supported comparisons with earlier surveys.
sentences.support: A total of 506 individuals responded to the survey.

sentences.text: The Commission concludes that the proportion seeing corruption as a major problem declined over the longer term, while awareness of the Commission remained high.
sentences.support: there appears to have been a long-term decline in the proportion of respondents who view corruption in NSW as a major problem.

sentences.text: The Commission found that most respondents were willing to report serious corruption, although only a slim majority expected useful action from a report.
sentences.support: A slim majority of respondents believes that reports of corruption will result in appropriate action.

findings.quote: Overall, there appears to have been a long-term decline in the proportion of respondents who view corruption in NSW as a major problem.
Most respondents appear willing to report serious corruption.

notes: No overall executive summary or formal recommendations list; conclusions appear in topic chapters. Survey attitudes and intentions are not presented as actual corruption levels or reporting behaviour.
